Assuming “last Tuesday” means **August 25, 2026**, my best answer is:

**Supported fact:** I found **no good web evidence of a new public Project Xanadu event on that date**. The Project Xanadu pages I found are old or archival in character: the main homepage includes a `crudcheck 01.05.23` marker and a “WE FIGHT ON” message, not a dated August 2026 announcement. https://www.xanadu.com/xuhome.html

**Supported fact:** One of the main public FAQ pages for Xanadu says `Last-modified: 2002/04/12`. https://www.aus.xanadu.com/xanadu/faq.html

**Supported fact:** A Xanadu demo page says it was created for the **Future of Text Conference, August 25, 2016**, and says, “We do not have a product, but a preliminary capability.” https://xanadu.com/xuDemoPage.html

**Supported fact:** The clearly dated **August 25, 2026** “Xanadu” news I did find was about **Xanadu Quantum Technologies** and Mitsubishi Chemical expanding a quantum-semiconductor collaboration, not about **Project Xanadu**. https://investors.xanadu.ai/news-releases/news-release-details/canada-japan-funding-fuels-xanadu-and-mitsubishi-chemical  
https://thequantuminsider.com/2026/08/25/xanadu-mitsubishi-quantum-semiconductor-manufacturing/

## Bottom line

I found **no evidence that anything notable happened to Project Xanadu — Ted Nelson's hypertext project — last Tuesday.** The premise of the question appears to be unsupported. Because there is no established event, there is also no "why" to explain.

"Last Tuesday" relative to today (Thursday, 2026-08-27) is **2026-08-25**; I also checked the prior Tuesday, 2026-08-18, in case that was meant.

## What I checked, and what I found

**Supported facts (negative findings):**

- Project Xanadu's Wikipedia article was last edited 13 August 2026, and its most recent dated project milestone remains **OpenXanadu in 2014** — nothing from August 2026 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Xanadu)).
- Ted Nelson is still recorded as living (born 17 June 1937, age 89), with no death date; that article was last edited 3 August 2026 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Nelson)). So the common guess — an obituary — is not supported.
- The project's site xanadu.com is still up and presents the project in its usual form, with no shutdown or release notice ([xanadu.com](https://www.xanadu.com/xuhome.html)).
- Targeted searches for Xanadu/Ted Nelson news dated 18 or 25 August 2026 returned only historical material (e.g., the 1999 Slashdot item on Nelson releasing the Xanadu source, and a 2014 podcast episode) — nothing current ([Slashdot, 1999](https://slashdot.org/story/99/08/25/0829248/ted-nelson-releases-xanadu)).

**The only thing I found actually dated Tuesday 2026-08-25 involving the hypertext Xanadu** is a Hacker News submission of the old Xanadu paper *"Back to the Future: Hypertext the Way It Used to Be"* ([xanadu.net](https://www.xanadu.net/XanaduSpace/btf.htm)), posted 2026-08-25T17:21Z by user GaryBluto, which received **6 points and 0 comments** ([HN item 49437459](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49437459)). That is a link-sharing event with essentially no traction, not something that "happened to" the project. I mention it only for completeness.

## Most likely source of the confusion (inference, not fact)

There is a **name collision**. On Tuesday 2026-08-25, **Xanadu Quantum Technologies** (a Toronto photonic-quantum-computing company, ticker XNDU — unrelated to Nelson's project) announced the next phase of its collaboration with Mitsubishi Chemical on simulating EUV lithography, funded by Canada's NRC IRAP and Japan's SIP program via AIST and G-QuAT ([GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/25/3350298/0/en/canada-japan-funding-fuels-xanadu-and-mitsubishi-chemical-partnership-on-quantum-semiconductor-research.html), [The Quantum Insider](https://thequantuminsider.com/2026/08/25/xanadu-mitsubishi-quantum-semiconductor-manufacturing/)). It also announced on 2026-08-24 a technological roadmap presentation set for 2026-08-31 ([GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/24/3350098/0/en/xanadu-announces-technological-roadmap-presentation.html)).

My inference — flagged as inference — is that a question about "Project Xanadu last Tuesday" most plausibly picked up this quantum-computing news. But that company is not called "Project Xanadu," so I can't assert that's what you meant.

## Uncertainty and limits

- I found no disagreement between sources; the issue is **absence of evidence**, not conflicting evidence.
- My coverage relies on web search indexing plus HN's API. A low-visibility event — a mailing-list post, a talk, a site change not yet indexed — could exist and not surface this way. Absence of evidence here is fairly strong for anything newsworthy, but not conclusive for something small.
- If you have a source or a hint (a headline, a platform, a person), tell me and I'll chase it directly.
